name: red-1
purpose: RED: the HTTP-level behavioral tests of C022 (tenant isolation, session lifecycle, refusals, pipelining in this process and in a separate one) run against the RETAINED NAIVE STUB (evidence/red/stub/server.cjs: tenant from a client claim, one global table, shared ETags, session fixation, no logout/revoke effect, stale roles, replayable tickets, id echoed in errors, mass assignment, no close after a refusal). Every failure is an assertion about the specified behavior.

notOk: the audit trail is per tenant: a denial or a probe is recorded in the caller tenant only, anonymous refusals in no tenant
one user flooding denials cannot evict the record of another user or of another tenant
quota exhaustion in one tenant starves nobody else: projects and sessions
mass assignment: a body can never set a role, a tenant, an owner, an id or a version; the owner is the verified user
two credentials, a lowercase scheme and an empty value are handled by one strict rule
a tenant named in ANY header, query field or body field is refused whatever its value, and nothing changes
IDOR on projects: an id that exists only in the OTHER tenant is answered exactly like an id that exists nowhere, in both directions, for every verb
IDOR on profiles, session handles and users: foreign ids are answered like missing ones and nothing changes
a user who belongs to two tenants acts in ONE of them per session: the role change of one tenant never touches the other
the same resource id in two tenants never collides: content, ETags, edits and deletes are per tenant
conditional requests cannot cross tenants: an ETag of one tenant validates nothing in another and never turns a missing id into 304
every answer is private to the caller: no-store, Vary Authorization, never a cookie, and a decoy cookie changes nothing
lists, counts, search and cursors show the caller tenant only; a cursor of another tenant is refused like a garbled one
anonymous to authenticated: the session id AND the token change at login, and the anonymous token is dead (no fixation)
a client can neither choose nor adopt a session id: a body naming one is refused, a header or cookie is not an identity channel, a refusal consumes nothing
a login ticket is ONE-TIME: replay, expiry, an unknown or malformed ticket and a session token as a ticket are all TICKET_INVALID
an authenticated session cannot log in again (that would be a tenant switch without logging out): 409 and the ticket stays unspent
logout ends the session for good: the dead token is refused everywhere, a second logout too, and a new login is a new session
an admin revokes by session id or by user: the token is refused at once; revoking what already ended is a refusal
a session expires by the injected clock and never revives; the state an admin sees is derived, not written by a refused request
tenant switch needs a fresh authentication: a request, a claim, or the old token never moves a session; a new login is a separate session
every illegal transition is a typed refusal with NO effect on the world
